001.statement: Binary numbers use only the digits 0 and 1.
001.explanation: Binary is base 2, so its only digits are 0 and 1.

002.statement: The unsigned binary number 00101101 is 46 in denary.

004.statement: Hexadecimal 3C is equivalent to 48 in denary.

005.statement: A character set assigns codes to characters.
005.explanation: A character set defines the characters and corresponding codes used to represent them.

006.statement: Image metadata is the binary colour code for every pixel.
006.correction: Metadata stores additional details about an image, such as its width, height or colour depth.
006.explanation: Pixel colour data and image metadata have different purposes.

007.statement: An audio sample rate of 8,000 Hz means 8,000 samples are taken every second.
007.explanation: Hertz measures samples per second in this context.

008.statement: Lossy compression always lets you restore source code exactly.
008.correction: Lossless compression can restore the original exactly; lossy compression discards information.
008.explanation: Losing even one source-code character could change or break a program.

009.statement: RAM holds active program instructions and working data while a program runs.
009.explanation: The CPU can access instructions and data currently held in RAM.

010.statement: USB flash drives store data on spinning magnetic disks.
010.correction: USB flash drives use solid-state flash memory.
010.explanation: They do not use a moving read/write mechanism.

011.statement: The Memory Address Register (MAR) holds the address of a memory location being accessed.
011.explanation: The MAR holds an address, not the data stored at that address.

012.statement: A higher CPU clock speed guarantees that every program runs faster.
012.correction: A higher clock speed means more cycles per second, but performance also depends on other factors.
012.explanation: Comparing performance requires considering cores, cache, architecture and the task.

013.statement: Abstraction removes irrelevant details while keeping what is needed to solve a problem.
013.explanation: Abstraction focuses on the information needed for the task.

014.statement: Sequence means program instructions can execute in any order.
014.correction: Sequence means instructions execute in the specified order.
014.explanation: Changing the order can change a program's result.

015.statement: A linear search requires the list to be sorted before it can work.
015.correction: Linear search can work on an unsorted list.
015.explanation: It checks items one at a time until it finds a match or reaches the end.

016.statement: In ascending bubble sort, adjacent items swap when the left value is greater than the right.
016.explanation: Swapping out-of-order adjacent pairs moves larger values towards the end.

017.statement: Assigning a new value to a variable leaves its previous value unchanged.
017.correction: Assignment stores the new value, replacing the previous value.
017.explanation: For example, x = 5 followed by x = 7 leaves x holding 7.

018.statement: Input validation checks whether data meets rules, not whether the information is factually true.
018.explanation: A value can pass a range or format check and still be incorrect in real life.

019.statement: Testing with suitable inputs can reveal errors in a program or algorithm.
019.explanation: Normal, boundary and invalid test data can expose different faults.

020.statement: If club = "Chess", print(club) displays the word club.
020.explanation: Without quotation marks in print(club), Python prints the value held in the variable.

021.statement: A thermostat controller is an embedded system designed for a specific temperature-control task.
021.explanation: It is part of a larger heating system and performs a dedicated task.

022.statement: A LAN must connect devices across several countries.
022.correction: A LAN connects devices across a relatively small local area.
022.explanation: A school site is a typical example of a LAN.

023.statement: In a client-server network, servers provide resources or services requested by clients.
023.explanation: Servers can centrally manage shared resources such as files and logins.

024.statement: A network interface card (NIC) is a device's backup storage system.
024.correction: A NIC provides the interface that lets a device connect to a network.
024.explanation: Networking and data backup are different functions.

025.statement: DNS helps find the IP address associated with a domain name.
025.explanation: DNS resolves a domain name to address records used to contact the destination.
